sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtāhnikāḥ sarve divyacandanarūṣitāḥ kalyāṇamanasaś caiva brāhmaṇān svasti vācya ca
english: Then, having completed their daily rites, all anointed with divine sandalwood, their minds set on auspiciousness, they invoked blessings from the brahmins.

sanskrit: manojñam aśanaṃ bhuktvā viviśuḥ śaraṇāny atha upagīyamānā nārībhir asvapan kurunandanāḥ
english: Having eaten delightful food, they then retired to their apartments; the sons of Kuru slept, serenaded by women singing.

sanskrit: jagāma teṣāṃ sā rātriḥ puṇyā rativihāriṇām stūyamānāś ca viśrāntāḥ kāle nidrām athātyajan
english: That auspicious night passed for them as they reveled in pleasure; praised by bards, they rested, and in due time abandoned sleep.

sanskrit: sukhoṣitās tāṃ rajanīṃ prātaḥ sarve kṛtāhnikāḥ sabhāṃ ramyāṃ praviviśuḥ kitavair abhisaṃvṛtām
english: Having spent that night in comfort, at dawn all completed their morning rites and entered the beautiful assembly hall, thronged with gamblers.

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca upastīrṇā sabhā rājan rantuṃ caite kṛtakṣaṇāḥ akṣān uptvā devanasya samayo 'stu yudhiṣṭhira
english: Śakuni said: O king, the hall is spread and ready; these men have appointed the time for play. Having cast the dice, let the moment of gambling be now, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca nikṛtir devanaṃ pāpaṃ na kṣātro 'tra parākramaḥ na ca nītir dhruvā rājan kiṃ tvaṃ dyūtaṃ praśaṃsasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Gambling through trickery is sinful; there is no warrior's valor in it, nor is there any firm statecraft, O king. Why then do you praise dicing?

sanskrit: na hi mānaṃ praśaṃsanti nikṛtau kitavasya ha śakune maiva no jaiṣīr amārgeṇa nṛśaṃsavat
english: They do not praise the honor of a gambler who wins through trickery. O Śakuni, do not defeat us by crooked means, like a cruel wretch.

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca yo 'nveti saṃkhyāṃ nikṛtau vidhijñaś; ceṣṭāsv akhinnaḥ kitavo 'kṣajāsu mahāmatir yaś ca jānāti dyūtaṃ; sa vai sarvaṃ sahate prakriyāsu
english: Śakuni said: One who is versed in the science of trickery, who is tireless in the movements of dice, the great-minded gambler who knows the game — he endures all its procedures.

sanskrit: akṣaglahaḥ so 'bhibhavet paraṃ nas; tenaiva kālo bhavatīdam āttha dīvyāmahe pārthiva mā viśaṅkāṃ; kuruṣva pāṇaṃ ca ciraṃ ca mā kṛthāḥ
english: Such a master of dice will overcome our opponents; that is the moment for this, as you yourself say. O prince, let us gamble — have no fear; set your stake and do not delay.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca evam āhāyam asito devalo munisattamaḥ imāni lokadvārāṇi yo vai saṃcarate sadā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Thus spoke the foremost of sages, the sage Asita Devala — that one who always moves through these gates of the world:

sanskrit: idaṃ vai devanaṃ pāpaṃ māyayā kitavaiḥ saha dharmeṇa tu jayo yuddhe tat paraṃ sādhu devanam
english: "This gambling with trickery among gamblers is sinful; but victory in battle by righteousness — that is the best and proper contest."

sanskrit: nāryā mlecchanti bhāṣābhir māyayā na caranty uta ajihmam aśaṭhaṃ yuddham etat satpuruṣavratam
english: Warriors do not stoop to barbarous speech or deceit; straightforward and guileless combat — this is the vow of noble men.

sanskrit: śaktito brāhmaṇān vandyāñ śikṣituṃ prayatāmahe tad vai vittaṃ mātidevīr mā jaiṣīḥ śakune param
english: To the best of our ability we strive to honor brahmins worthy of reverence and to learn from them — that is true wealth, O goddess of fortune. Do not defeat us further, O Śakuni.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ nikṛtyā kāmaye sukhāny uta dhanāni vā kitavasyāpy anikṛter vṛttam etan na pūjyate
english: I do not desire pleasures or wealth through deceit; even for a gambler, conduct without trickery is what is not honored — yet I will not adopt it.

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca śrotriyo 'śrotriyam uta nikṛtyaiva yudhiṣṭhira vidvān aviduṣo 'bhyeti nāhus tāṃ nikṛtiṃ janāḥ
english: Śakuni said: A learned man approaches an unlearned man, O Yudhiṣṭhira, and a wise man approaches a fool — people do not call that trickery.

sanskrit: evaṃ tvaṃ mām ihābhyetya nikṛtiṃ yadi manyase devanād vinivartasva yadi te vidyate bhayam
english: If you consider me approaching you here to be trickery, then turn away from gambling, if you have any fear.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca āhūto na nivarteyam iti me vratam āhitam vidhiś ca balavān rājan diṣṭasyāsmi vaśe sthitaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When summoned, I will not turn back — this is the vow I have undertaken; and fate is powerful, O king. I stand under the control of destiny.

sanskrit: asmin samāgame kena devanaṃ me bhaviṣyati pratipāṇaś ca ko 'nyo 'sti tato dyūtaṃ pravartatām
english: In this assembly, with whom shall I gamble, and who else is there to counter-stake? Then let the gambling commence.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca ahaṃ dātāsmi ratnānāṃ dhanānāṃ ca viśāṃ pate madarthe devitā cāyaṃ śakunir mātulo mama
english: Duryodhana said: I shall be the provider of gems and wealth, O lord of men; and on my behalf this Śakuni, my maternal uncle, shall play.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca anyenānyasya viṣamaṃ devanaṃ pratibhāti me etad vidvann upādatsva kāmam evaṃ pravartatām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: For one person to gamble on behalf of another seems unfair to me. O learned one, accept this understanding — so let it proceed accordingly.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca upohyamāne dyūte tu rājānaḥ sarva eva te dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ puraskṛtya viviśus tāṃ sabhāṃ tataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the gambling was about to begin, all those kings, placing Dhṛtarāṣṭra at their head, then entered that assembly hall.

sanskrit: bhīṣmo droṇaḥ kṛpaś caiva viduraś ca mahāmatiḥ nātīvaprītamanasas te 'nvavartanta bhārata
english: Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, and the great-minded Vidura followed, their hearts not entirely at ease, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: te dvaṃdvaśaḥ pṛthak caiva siṃhagrīvā mahaujasaḥ siṃhāsanāni bhūrīṇi vicitrāṇi ca bhejire
english: Those lion-necked, mighty-spirited ones took their places, each separately and in pairs, upon the many splendid and variegated lion-thrones.

sanskrit: śuśubhe sā sabhā rājan rājabhis taiḥ samāgataiḥ devair iva mahābhāgaiḥ samavetais triviṣṭapam
english: That assembly hall shone beautifully, O king, with those kings assembled — like heaven resplendent with the greatly blessed gods gathered together.

sanskrit: sarve vedavidaḥ śūrāḥ sarve bhāsvaramūrtayaḥ prāvartata mahārāja suhṛddyūtam anantaram
english: All were knowers of the Vedas, all were heroes, all of brilliant form. Then, O great king, the gambling among friends commenced.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ayaṃ bahudhano rājan sāgarāvartasaṃbhavaḥ maṇir hārottaraḥ śrīmān kanakottamabhūṣaṇaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This gem, O king, born from the whirlpools of the ocean, excelling a necklace, splendid and adorned with the finest gold, is of great worth.

sanskrit: etad rājan dhanaṃ mahyaṃ pratipāṇas tu kas tava bhavatv eṣa kramas tāta jayāmy enaṃ durodaram
english: This, O king, is my stake — now what is your counter-stake? Let this be the order, my friend; I will win this wager.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca santi me maṇayaś caiva dhanāni vividhāni ca matsaraś ca na me 'rtheṣu jayāmy enaṃ durodaram
english: Duryodhana said: I have gems and various riches too, and I have no greed for wealth. I will win this wager.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato jagrāha śakunis tān akṣān akṣatattvavit jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Śakuni, who knew the truth of dice, took those dice; and Śakuni spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won!"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mattaḥ kaitavakenaiva yaj jito 'smi durodaram śakune hanta dīvyāmo glahamānāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Though I have been defeated by your dice-trick, O Śakuni, come — let us gamble, staking thousands.

sanskrit: ime niṣkasahasrasya kuṇḍino bharitāḥ śatam kośo hiraṇyam akṣayyaṃ jātarūpam anekaśaḥ etad rājan dhanaṃ mahyaṃ tena dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: These hundred jars each filled with a thousand niṣkas, a treasury of inexhaustible gold, refined gold in many forms — this, O king, is my wealth; with this I gamble against you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktaḥ śakuniḥ prāha jitam ity eva taṃ nṛpam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, Śakuni said to that king: "Won!"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ayaṃ sahasrasamito vaiyāghraḥ supravartitaḥ sucakropaskaraḥ śrīmān kiṅkiṇījālamaṇḍitaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This tiger-chariot, worth a thousand, excellently fitted out, furnished with fine wheels, splendid, adorned with a network of bells —

sanskrit: saṃhrādano rājaratho ya ihāsmān upāvahat jaitro rathavaraḥ puṇyo meghasāgaraniḥsvanaḥ
english: — this royal chariot that brought us here, resounding like thunder, the best of victorious chariots, sacred, its roar like that of clouds and ocean —

sanskrit: aṣṭau yaṃ kuraracchāyāḥ sadaśvā rāṣṭrasaṃmatāḥ vahanti naiṣām ucyeta padā bhūmim upaspṛśan etad rājan dhanaṃ mahyaṃ tena dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: — eight osprey-hued horses, acclaimed by the realm, draw it; not one of them can be said to touch the ground with its foot. This, O king, is my wealth; with this I gamble against you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this, resolute and resorting to trickery, Śakuni said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won!"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sahasrasaṃkhyā nāgā me mattās tiṣṭhanti saubala hemakakṣāḥ kṛtāpīḍāḥ padmino hemamālinaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have a thousand elephants, in rut, standing ready, O son of Subala — with golden girths, adorned with ornaments, bearing lotus-marks, garlanded with gold.

sanskrit: sudāntā rājavahanāḥ sarvaśabdakṣamā yudhi īṣādantā mahākāyāḥ sarve cāṣṭakareṇavaḥ
english: Well-trained, fit to bear kings, able to endure all sounds in battle, with tusk-like teeth, of great body, each standing eight cubits tall.

sanskrit: sarve ca purabhettāro nagameghanibhā gajāḥ etad rājan dhanaṃ mahyaṃ tena dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: All of them breakers of city-gates, those elephants resembling mountain-clouds — this, O king, is my wealth; with this I gamble against you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tam evaṃvādinaṃ pārthaṃ prahasann iva saubalaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: To that Pārtha speaking thus, the son of Subala, as if laughing, said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won!"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śataṃ dāsīsahasrāṇi taruṇyo me prabhadrikāḥ kambukeyūradhāriṇyo niṣkakaṇṭhyaḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have a hundred thousand maidservants, young and auspicious, wearing conch-shell bracelets and armlets, adorned with gold necklaces, well-ornamented.

sanskrit: mahārhamālyābharaṇāḥ suvastrāś candanokṣitāḥ maṇīn hema ca bibhratyaḥ sarvā vai sūkṣmavāsasaḥ
english: Wearing precious garlands and ornaments, clothed in fine garments, anointed with sandalwood, bearing gems and gold — all clad in fine silken robes.

sanskrit: anusevāṃ carantīmāḥ kuśalā nṛtyasāmasu snātakānām amātyānāṃ rājñāṃ ca mama śāsanāt etad rājan dhanaṃ mahyaṃ tena dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: These women skilled in dance and song perform services at my command for learned scholars, ministers, and kings. This, O king, is my wealth; with this I gamble against you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this, resolute and resorting to trickery, Śakuni said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won!"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca etāvanty eva dāsānāṃ sahasrāṇy uta santi me pradakṣiṇānulomāś ca prāvāravasanāḥ sadā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have that many thousands of male servants too — devoted and agreeable, always clothed in fine cloaks.

sanskrit: prājñā medhāvino dakṣā yuvāno mṛṣṭakuṇḍalāḥ pātrīhastā divārātram atithīn bhojayanty uta etad rājan dhanaṃ mahyaṃ tena dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: Wise, intelligent, skilled, young, wearing polished earrings, holding serving-vessels in hand, they feed guests day and night. This, O king, is my wealth; with this I gamble against you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this, resolute and resorting to trickery, Śakuni said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won!"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca rathās tāvanta eveme hemabhāṇḍāḥ patākinaḥ hayair vinītaiḥ saṃpannā rathibhiś citrayodhibhiḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have that many chariots too — fitted with golden equipment, bearing banners, furnished with trained horses and skilled chariot-fighters of varied combat.

sanskrit: ekaiko yatra labhate sahasraparamāṃ bhṛtim yudhyato 'yudhyato vāpi vetanaṃ māsakālikam etad rājan dhanaṃ mahyaṃ tena dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: Each of these receives wages of at most a thousand, whether in battle or not, paid monthly. This, O king, is my wealth; with this I gamble against you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity evam ukte pārthena kṛtavairo durātmavān jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Pārtha had spoken thus, that evil-spirited one who had created enmity said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won!"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca aśvāṃs tittirikalmāṣān gāndharvān hemamālinaḥ dadau citrarathas tuṣṭo yāṃs tān gāṇḍīvadhanvane etad rājan dhanaṃ mahyaṃ tena dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The horses, spotted like partridges, of Gandharva breed, garlanded with gold, which Citraratha, delighted, gave to the bearer of the Gāṇḍīva bow — this, O king, is my wealth; with this I gamble against you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this, resolute and resorting to trickery, Śakuni said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won!"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca rathānāṃ śakaṭānāṃ ca hayānāṃ cāyutāni me yuktānām eva tiṣṭhanti vāhair uccāvacair vṛtāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have ten thousand chariots, carts, and horses, kept in readiness, surrounded by draft animals of various kinds.

sanskrit: evaṃ varṇasya varṇasya samuccīya sahasraśaḥ kṣīraṃ pibantas tiṣṭhanti bhuñjānāḥ śālitaṇḍulān
english: Gathered by caste from each caste in their thousands, they stand drinking milk and eating rice of the finest grain.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭis tāni sahasrāṇi sarve pṛthulavakṣasaḥ etad rājan dhanaṃ mahyaṃ tena dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: Sixty thousand of them, all broad-chested — this, O king, is my wealth; with this I gamble against you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this, resolute and resorting to trickery, Śakuni said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won!"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca tāmralohaiḥ parivṛtā nidhayo me catuḥśatāḥ pañcadrauṇika ekaikaḥ suvarṇasyāhatasya vai etad rājan dhanaṃ mahyaṃ tena dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have four hundred treasure-chests encased in copper and iron, each containing five droṇas of unworked gold. This, O king, is my wealth; with this I gamble against you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this, resolute and resorting to trickery, Śakuni said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won!"

sanskrit: vidura uvāca mahārāja vijānīhi yat tvāṃ vakṣyāmi tac chṛṇu mumūrṣor auṣadham iva na rocetāpi te śrutam
english: Vidura said: O great king, understand and hear what I shall tell you — though it may not please you when heard, like medicine to a dying man.

sanskrit: yad vai purā jātamātro rurāva; gomāyuvad visvaraṃ pāpacetāḥ duryodhano bhāratānāṃ kulaghnaḥ; so 'yaṃ yukto bhavitā kālahetuḥ
english: When he was just born, that evil-minded Duryodhana, destroyer of the Bhārata line, howled like a jackal with a discordant cry — this same one is fated to be the instrument of death.

sanskrit: gṛhe vasantaṃ gomāyuṃ tvaṃ vai matvā na budhyase duryodhanasya rūpeṇa śṛṇu kāvyāṃ giraṃ mama
english: You keep a jackal dwelling in your house, yet you do not realize it under Duryodhana's form. Listen to my wise counsel.

sanskrit: madhu vai mādhviko labdhvā prapātaṃ nāvabudhyate āruhya taṃ majjati vā patanaṃ vādhigacchati
english: A honey-seeker, having obtained honey, does not perceive the precipice; climbing upon it, he either sinks or meets his fall.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ matto 'kṣadevena madhuvan na parīkṣate prapātaṃ budhyate naiva vairaṃ kṛtvā mahārathaiḥ
english: This Duryodhana, intoxicated with gambling as with honey, does not examine the precipice; he does not at all perceive the enmity he is creating with the great warriors.

sanskrit: viditaṃ te mahārāja rājasv evāsamañjasam andhakā yādavā bhojāḥ sametāḥ kaṃsam atyajan
english: You know it, O great king — it is improper even among kings: the Andhakas, Yādavas, and Bhojas, gathered together, abandoned Kaṃsa.

sanskrit: niyogāc ca hate tasmin kṛṣṇenāmitraghātinā evaṃ te jñātayaḥ sarve modamānāḥ śataṃ samāḥ
english: And when he was slain by Kṛṣṇa, the slayer of enemies, at the bidding of all, then all your kinsmen rejoiced for a hundred years.

sanskrit: tvanniyuktaḥ savyasācī nigṛhṇātu suyodhanam nigrahād asya pāpasya modantāṃ kuravaḥ sukham
english: Let Savyasācī, commissioned by you, restrain Suyodhana; by restraining this wicked one, let the Kurus rejoice in happiness.

sanskrit: kākenemāṃś citrabarhāñ śārdūlān kroṣṭukena ca krīṇīṣva pāṇḍavān rājan mā majjīḥ śokasāgare
english: Would you exchange these Pāṇḍavas — peacocks — for a crow or a jackal, O king? Do not sink into an ocean of grief.

sanskrit: tyajet kulārthe puruṣaṃ grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet grāmaṃ janapadasyārthe ātmārthe pṛthivīṃ tyajet
english: For the sake of the family one should abandon an individual; for the sake of the village, abandon the family; for the sake of the kingdom, abandon the village; for the sake of the self, abandon the earth.

sanskrit: sarvajñaḥ sarvabhāvajñaḥ sarvaśatrubhayaṃkaraḥ iti sma bhāṣate kāvyo jambhatyāge mahāsurān
english: "Omniscient, knowing all conditions, terrifying to all enemies" — thus spoke Uśanas Kāvya when Indra was to be abandoned for the great demons.

sanskrit: hiraṇyaṣṭhīvinaḥ kaś cit pakṣiṇo vanagocarān gṛhe kila kṛtāvāsāṃl lobhād rājann apīḍayat
english: O king, a certain man who kept forest-roaming birds that voided gold in his house oppressed them out of greed.

sanskrit: sadopabhojyāṃl lobhāndho hiraṇyārthe paraṃtapa āyatiṃ ca tadātvaṃ ca ubhe sadyo vyanāśayat
english: Blinded by greed for gold, he destroyed what was perpetually to be enjoyed, O scorcher of foes — both future profit and present gain he destroyed at once.

sanskrit: tadātvakāmaḥ pāṇḍūṃs tvaṃ mā druho bharatarṣabha mohātmā tapyase paścāt pakṣihā puruṣo yathā
english: Greedy for present gain, do not harm the Pāṇḍavas, O bull of the Bhāratas; deluded in spirit, you will repent afterward, like the man who killed the birds.

sanskrit: jātaṃ jātaṃ pāṇḍavebhyaḥ puṣpam ādatsva bhārata mālākāra ivārāme snehaṃ kurvan punaḥ punaḥ
english: Gather the fruit as it arises from the Pāṇḍavas, O Bhārata — like a gardener in a garden, showing affection again and again.

sanskrit: vṛkṣān aṅgārakārīva mainān dhākṣīḥ samūlakān mā gamaḥ sasutāmātyaḥ sabalaś ca parābhavam
english: Do not burn them down to the roots like a charcoal-maker burning trees; do not go with your sons, ministers, and army toward ruin.

sanskrit: samavetān hi kaḥ pārthān pratiyudhyeta bhārata marudbhiḥ sahito rājann api sākṣān marutpatiḥ
english: For who could fight the Pārthas assembled together, O Bhārata? Not even Indra himself, O king, accompanied by the Maruts.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca dyūtaṃ mūlaṃ kalahasyānupāti; mithobhedāya mahate vā raṇāya yad āsthito 'yaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putro; duryodhanaḥ sṛjate vairam ugram
english: Vidura said: Gambling is the root of strife that follows — leading to great mutual division or to war. Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, who has set himself on this course, Duryodhana creates fierce enmity.

sanskrit: prātipīyāḥ śāṃtanavā bhaimasenāḥ sabāhlikāḥ duryodhanāparādhena kṛcchraṃ prāpsyanti sarvaśaḥ
english: The descendants of Prātīpa, the sons of Śāntanu, the sons of Bhīmasena, and those with Bāhlika — all shall encounter grave peril because of Duryodhana's offense.

sanskrit: duryodhano madenaiva kṣemaṃ rāṣṭrād apohati viṣāṇaṃ gaur iva madāt svayam ārujate balāt
english: Duryodhana, through sheer arrogance, pushes away the welfare of the kingdom; like a bull in rut he forcibly breaks off his own horn.

sanskrit: yaś cittam anveti parasya rājan; vīraḥ kaviḥ svām atipatya dṛṣṭim nāvaṃ samudra iva bālanetrām; āruhya ghore vyasane nimajjet
english: One who, O king, follows another's mind — a hero and a sage — overstepping his own sight, would board a ship steered by a child on the ocean, and in terrible disaster would drown.

sanskrit: duryodhano glahate pāṇḍavena; priyāyase tvaṃ jayatīti tac ca atinarmāj jāyate saṃprahāro; yato vināśaḥ samupaiti puṃsām
english: Duryodhana gambles against the Pāṇḍava; you are pleased when he wins — yet from excessive jest arises violent conflict, from which destruction comes upon men.
